summary: harness gc first stops the units of this project's runs with no live driver (+ stopped <u> (<run> ended|: driver gone), --dry-run would:, ? for no run of this project); harness status lists a running run's units with MemoryCurrent. scope_owns in lib/scope.sh is the shared match; stub systemctl answers MemoryCurrent and the described list-units shape.
verified_how: tests/run.sh 282 → 285/285 (scope_owns unit check, gc unit check with a.b/a-b collision decoy, status check in the termed block); the three failed before the code; lib/check.sh green in 493 s; Opus review of the diff, findings 1-3 and 5 fixed

dead_ends.tried: a waited `sleep 0` pid as the dead driver.pid
dead_ends.why: a reused pid would count as live (review): 999999999 is over any pid_max

discoveries.text: gc's unit step runs first in cmd_gc, before the fetch: a review found an offline fetch or a prunable worktree ends gc under set -e before a later step, and a worktree could be removed while a SIGKILLed run's session still ran in it. L4's per-worktree error handling should keep that order.

scope_owns <run> <unit>.scope (lib/scope.sh) is the one unit→run match (roles s<n>, check-<pid>, svc); bin/harness now sources lib/scope.sh. L3's gc of tmux sessions can follow the same candidates-over-every-project pattern.
Not fixed (display only): two running runs whose ids reduce to one prefix (a.b, a-b) each list both runs' units in harness status.
One full-suite run failed 'queue holds an entry whose project has a live run' (its busy3 driver is a `sleep 3`); the next two runs passed unchanged: a timing flake under load.

questions: D1 default (decisions/2026-10-25-gc-orphan-units): harness status calls list-units without a scope_available probe first (a failing list-units gives nothing; the probe would start a transient scope per status). Keep it?
proposed_changes: L2-05 step 1: the unit step runs first in cmd_gc, not after the branch passes (review finding); its lines are gc's own, not act's; a run with no live driver qualifies with or without ended (plan §11).
